title: Sandu: The Three Poisons 2
content:
Wei Wuxian froze. "He passed away?"

The image of Lan Wangji—bathed in the flickering firelight, a quiet tear cutting down his cheek—flashed unbidden across his mind. The question slipped out before he could catch it: "How's Lan Zhan holding up?"

"How else? He went back," Jiang Cheng replied. "Father offered to send an escort with him to Gusu, but he turned it down flat. Looking at him, it felt like he’d been bracing for this for a long time. With the way the world’s burning right now, it’s not like anyone’s having an easier time than anyone else."

They settled back against the wooden balustrade. Wei Wuxian asked, "And what about Lan Xichen?"

"You know how the Wen Clan wanted to torch their Library Pavilion? Tens of thousands of ancient scrolls and musical scores. The Lan disciples managed to salvage a fraction of it, and they probably handed it all to Lan Xichen so he could run for it. Save whatever he could carry, or lose it all to the ash. At least, that’s what everyone’s guessing."

Wei Wuxian tilted his head back, staring up at the open sky. "Disgusting."

"Yeah," Jiang Cheng agreed bitterly. "The Wen Clan is sickening."

"Just how long are they going to keep throwing their weight around like this? There are so many clans—can't we all just band together and—"

Before he could finish, a chaotic rush of pounding footsteps echoed down the walkway. A pack of boys dressed in short, practical tunics came scrambling down the corridor like a troop of monkeys, hollering at the top of their lungs: "Da-shixiong!!!"

The Sixth Shidi was practically beaming. "Da-shixiong! You're alive!!!"

Wei Wuxian snapped, "What do you mean, 'I'm alive'?! I wasn't dead in the first place!"

"Da-shixiong, we heard you slayed a four-hundred-year-old monster! Is it true?! Did you really kill it?!"

"Forget that, I want to know if you actually went seven days without a bite to eat!"

"You didn't secretly fast and practice inedia behind our backs, did you?!"

"Just how massive was the Xuanwu of Slaughter?! Could it even fit inside Lotus Lake?!"

"The Xuanwu of Slaughter is just a giant bastard of a turtle, right?!"

"Da-shixiong, you spent a whole week trapped with Lan Wangji from Gusu?! How did he not beat you to death?!"

The heavy gloom from moments ago was instantly shattered, scattered to the wind by pure, unadulterated teenage chaos.

Wei Wuxian’s injuries hadn't been critically severe to begin with; they'd only worsened from lack of immediate treatment, utter exhaustion, and an empty stomach. But he was young and built of sturdy stuff. Once the salve was slathered over the brand on his chest, the fever broke in no time. After lounging in bed for a few days, he was back on his feet, practically bursting with energy.

Following the bloodbath with the Xuanwu on Mount Muxi, the "Re-education Office" set up by the Wen Clan in Qishan fell apart entirely. The disciples from every sect had scattered back to their respective homes, and Wen Chao hadn't come knocking to settle scores just yet. Madam Yu had seized the chance to thoroughly tear into Wei Wuxian, forbidding him from taking a single step past the front gates of Lotus Pier—barring him even from rowing a boat out onto the lake. Left with no other choice, he spent his days shooting kites alongside the other Jiang disciples.

Even the most entertaining game grew stale when played every single day. Within two weeks, the boys' enthusiasm had thoroughly evaporated. Wei Wuxian couldn't be bothered either, tossing off sloppy, careless shots that miraculously let Jiang Cheng snag first place several times in a row.

That evening, as the final volley wrapped up, Wei Wuxian shaded his eyes with a hand, looking out over the fading amber glow of the sunset. "Pack it in. Let's call it a day and head inside for dinner."

Jiang Cheng raised a brow. "Calling it this early?"

Tossing his bow to the dirt, Wei Wuxian slumped down onto the boards, letting out a heavy sigh. "Boring. I'm over it. Who took the bottom ranks just now? Go trail behind Sixth Shidi and fetch the kites."

One of the boys protested, "Da-shixiong, you're so shameless! You always make everyone else fetch your kites. Total cheat."

Wei Wuxian waved a hand dismissively. "My hands are tied! Madam Yu barred me from stepping foot outside. She’s home right now—Jinzhu and Yinzhu are probably lurking around some corner watching my every move, waiting to rat me out. If I cross that threshold, Madam Yu will whip a whole layer of skin clean off my back."

The disciples who had scored dead last traded a few playful jabs, laughing as they sauntered out the gates to track down the fallen targets. Jiang Cheng remained standing while Wei Wuxian lounged on the deck. After trading a few idle comments, Wei Wuxian asked, "Uncle Jiang left early this morning, so why isn't he back yet? Will he make it in time for dinner?"

Jiang Fengmian and Madam Yu had gotten into another fight that morning. Well, calling it a fight wasn't entirely accurate; it was mostly Madam Yu venting her bitter rage in a one-sided tirade, while Jiang Fengmian quietly maintained an air of stoic restraint.

Jiang Cheng scowled, "He went back to the Wen Clan to negotiate for our swords, obviously. The thought of some Wen dog putting his filthy hands on Sandu makes my skin crawl..."

Disgust dripped from his face. Wei Wuxian mused, "Shame our blades don't have enough spiritual awareness. If they could seal themselves automatically, no one else would ever be able to draw them."

Jiang Cheng sneered, "Cultivate for another eighty years, and maybe you'll pull it off."

Suddenly, several young disciples came barreling back onto the training grounds, their shouts laced with raw panic: "Disaster! Da-shixiong, Shixiong, disaster!!!"

It was the very disciples who had just left to fetch the kites. Wei Wuxian sprang to his feet. "What happened?"

Jiang Cheng’s eyes swept the group. "Where's Sixth Shidi? Why is there one missing?"

Sure enough, Sixth Shidi had sprinted out the gates first, but now he was nowhere in sight. Out of breath and clutching his knees, a boy gasped, "Sixth Shidi... he was taken! Someone grabbed him!"

"Taken?!"

Wei Wuxian scooped his bow from the dirt, keeping the weapon firmly in his grip. "Who took him? Why the hell would anyone grab him?!"

"We don't know! We have no idea why they took him!"

Jiang Cheng’s temper flared. "What do you mean you don't know?!"

"Everyone calm down," Wei Wuxian intervened, his voice steadying the room. "Tell it slowly. What happened?"

The disciple stammered, "Just now... we went out to fetch the kites. They drifted super far away. By the time we tracked them down, we ran into a mob of dozens of people—Wen Clan members, wearing their signature robes! Disciples, retainers, and leading them was a young woman. She had a kite in her hands with an arrow through it, and the second she saw us, she demanded to know whose kite it was."

Another disciple chimed in, "The kite belonged to Sixth Shidi, so he just admitted it was his! The woman's face twisted instantly, screeching, 'How dare you!' and ordered her thugs to drag him off on the spot!"

Wei Wuxian frowned. "Just like that?"

The boys nodded frantically. "We asked why they were arresting him, but the woman just kept screaming that he was treasonous, harboring malicious intent, ordering her enforcers to haul him away! We had no way to fight them off, so we ran back!"

Jiang Cheng spat a furious curse. "Dragging people off without even an excuse?! Does the Wen Clan think they rule the heavens?!"

"Exactly! It makes zero sense!"

"Quiet, all of you," Wei Wuxian warned, his tone dropping low. "The Wens are probably right on your heels. Don't let them overhear anything they can twist into a handle against us. Let me ask you: was that woman unarmed? Fairly pretty, with a mole right above her lip?"

The disciples' eyes widened. "Yes! That was her!"

Jiang Cheng hissed through clenched teeth, "Wang Lingjiao! That vile..."

A sharp, frigid voice sliced through the commotion: "What is all this infernal noise?! Can I not get a single moment of peace in this house?!"

Draped in flowing purple silks, Madam Yu glided onto the veranda, flanked by Jinzhu and Yinzhu in full combat gear. Jiang Cheng stepped forward. "A-Niang, the Wens are here. They grabbed Sixth Shidi!"

Madam Yu scoffed, "You were screeching loudly enough that I heard every word from the inner halls. So what? He was dragged off, not struck dead on the spot! Stomping your feet, grinding your teeth, losing your head—is this how the future leader of a sect carries himself? Pull yourself together!"

With that, she turned to face the main gates. A dozen Wen cultivators draped in the blazing sunburst robes marched through in rigid succession. Strutting behind them came a woman adorned in vibrant, colorful silks, her hips swaying with exaggerated affectation.

She possessed a lithe, alluring figure and a flirtatious face, eyes brimming with coy glances and lips painted as red as fresh blood. A small, dark mole sat just above her lip—an undeniably striking beauty. Yet she was weighed down by a clattering mountain of gold hairpins and shimmering rings, as though desperately trying to wear an entire jewelry boutique and her master's doting favor all over her person, thoroughly cheapening her look. It was none other than Wang Lingjiao, whom Wei Wuxian had sent flying with a palm strike back on Mount Muxi.

Wang Lingjiao pursed her lips into a coy smile. "Madam Yu, here I am again."

Madam Yu stared back with cold detachment, as if deigning to offer a single word would soil her tongue. Wang Lingjiao descended the stone steps, and only then did Madam Yu speak: "What business do you have laying hands on a disciple of my Yunmeng Jiang Clan?"

"Laying hands?" Wang Lingjiao drawled. "You mean that boy outside? Well, that's quite a long story. Why don't we head inside, take our seats, and unpack it slowly?"

A mere housemaid, entering the ancestral gates of a prominent cultivation clan without announcement, without permission, and brazenly demanding to step into the main hall to 'sit down and unpack it slowly.' Madam Yu’s expression turned utterly lethal. The amethyst-studded ring on her right index finger sparked with two faint crackles of purple lightning, veins bulging subtly against the pale skin of her hand.

Her voice was dangerously quiet: "Go inside and sit down to talk?"

"Naturally," Wang Lingjiao replied breezily. "Last time I came to deliver orders, I didn't get the chance to sit. After you."

Hearing the phrase 'deliver orders', Jiang Cheng let out a low snarl, while Jinzhu and Yinzhu bristled with quiet fury. But Wang Lingjiao was currently Wen Chao's pampered darling; crossing her openly was out of the question. So, though Madam Yu’s face was coated in biting mockery and venomous contempt, she still stepped aside. "Very well. Step inside."

Flashing a radiant grin, Wang Lingjiao did just that.

Yet for all her talk of sitting down, she showed no rush to take a seat. Instead, she took a leisurely stroll around Lotus Pier, tossing out unsolicited critiques at every turn:

"This Lotus Pier isn't half bad. Huge, certainly, but the architecture feels horribly outdated."

"All this blackened wood... what an ugly, dreary color. It lacks vibrancy."

"Madam Yu, you really are lacking as the mistress of this house. Don't you know how to decorate? You should hang more crimson silk drapes next time. That would look far more fetching."

She ambled along, poking and prodding as if touring her own personal garden. Madam Yu’s brow twitched with an unhinged frequency, making Wei Wuxian and Jiang Cheng wonder if she was going to snap and slit the woman's throat on the spot.

Once her tour concluded, Wang Lingjiao finally sauntered into the main reception hall. Without waiting for an invitation or offering polite deferrals, she planted herself squarely in the head seat. After lounging there a moment and seeing no servants rushing forward, she scowled and slapped the tabletop. "Where is the tea?"

Despite her dazzling jewels, her manners were nonexistent—an absolute embarrassment from head to toe. By now, the onlookers had grown numb to the circus. Madam Yu settled into the secondary seat, her wide purple skirts cascading around her, accentuating her narrow waist and immaculate posture. Jinzhu and Yinzhu flanked her from behind, faint sneers tugging at their lips.

Yinzhu drawled, "There is no tea. If you want a drink, pour it yourself."

Wang Lingjiao’s eyes went wide with faux astonishment. "Do the Jiang Clan's servants never do their jobs?"

Jinzhu countered smoothly, "The servants of the Jiang Clan have actual responsibilities to attend to. Running around pouring tea is hardly a task that requires an escort. Unless, of course, one is crippled."

Wang Lingjiao swept her gaze over them. "And who are you two supposed to be?"

Madam Yu replied, "My personal handmaidens."

Wang Lingjiao scoffed with blatant disdain, "Madam Yu, your Jiang Clan truly has no sense of propriety. This simply won't do—allowing mere maids to brazenly run their mouths in the main hall? In the Wen Clan, servants like this would have their faces slapped raw."

Says the glorified servant girl herself, Wei Wuxian thought dryly.

Madam Yu remained unmoving as a stone wall. "Jinzhu and Yinzhu are no ordinary servants. They have been at my side since childhood. They answer to no one beneath the heavens except me, and no one has the standing to lay a hand on them. Not a soul can, and not a soul dares."

Wang Lingjiao sniffed, "Madam Yu, what kind of talk is that? In a proper clan, the boundary between master and servant must be etched in stone, otherwise chaos reigns. A servant ought to act like a servant."

Surprisingly, Madam Yu found herself deeply agreeing with that exact sentiment. She cast a pointed, lingering glance at Wei Wuxian, nodding with icy pride. "Indeed."

Then, her tone sharpened: "Now tell me: why did you seize a disciple of my house?"

Wang Lingjiao waved a flippant hand. "Madam Yu would do well to cut ties with that boy immediately. He harbors treacherous designs; I caught him red-handed and had him hauled off for sentencing."

Madam Yu raised an arched brow. "Treacherous designs?"

Jiang Cheng couldn't hold back: "What treacherous designs could Sixth Shidi possibly harbor?!"

"I have proof," Wang Lingjiao declared. "Bring it here!"

A Wen disciple stepped forward, presenting a battered kite. Wang Lingjiao shook it out by the struts. "Here is your evidence."

Wei Wuxian let out a derisive snort. "That's just a standard one-eyed monster painted on a kite. How is that evidence of anything?"

Wang Lingjiao sneered, "Do you think I'm blind? Look closely."

Her long index fingers, painted in vivid red polish, traced across the paper, launching into a smug, self-satisfied breakdown: "What color is this kite? Golden. And what shape is this one-eyed monster? Circular."

Madam Yu asked coldly, "And?"

"And?!" Wang Lingjiao gasped, feigning disbelief. "Madam Yu, haven't you pieced it together yet? Golden. Circular. What does that look like? —The Sun!"

While the room stared at her in deadpan shock, she puffed out her chest, thoroughly proud of her deduction: "Out of all the kites in the world, why did he have to make a one-eyed monster? Why did it have to be gold? Couldn't he have picked another shape? Couldn't it have been another color? Are you going to tell me this is a coincidence? Of course not! The boy did this deliberately! Launching a kite like this was an intentional metaphor for 'Shooting the Sun'! He wants to shoot down the sun! That is blatant, unforgivable disrespect toward the Qishan Wen Clan—if that isn't harboring treacherous designs, what is?!"

Watching her perform this convoluted mental gymnastics with such smug self-righteousness, Jiang Cheng snapped, "Even if that kite is round and gold, it looks nothing like a sun! It doesn't even resemble it in the slightest!"

Wei Wuxian chimed in, "By that logic, you might as well ban people from eating oranges. Aren't oranges round and golden too? Pretty sure I've seen you choke down more than a few."

Wang Lingjiao shot him a venomous glare.

Madam Yu’s voice was pure winter frost: "So you barged into my home purely over a kite?"

"Of course not," Wang Lingjiao replied. "I came today representing the Wen Clan and Young Master Wen, to punish an offender."

Wei Wuxian’s gut tightened.

Sure enough, a heartbeat later, Wang Lingjiao’s finger snapped around to point directly at him. "This brat! Back on Mount Muxi, while Young Master Wen was valiantly battling the Xuanwu of Slaughter, he hurled brazen insults, disrupted the fight at every turn, exhausted Young Master Wen to the brink of collapse, and even caused him to lose his personal spiritual sword!"

Hearing her brazenly flip black into white with such outrageous lies, Jiang Cheng let out a furious, incredulous laugh. Wei Wuxian, on the other hand, recalled Jiang Fengmian leaving at the crack of dawn. They picked this timing on purpose, he realized. Or they deliberately baited Uncle Jiang away from Lotus Pier!

Wang Lingjiao pressed on, "Fortunately, heaven blessed Young Master Wen! Even after losing his blade, he still brought down the Xuanwu of Slaughter without further mishap! But this little delinquent cannot be forgiven! I have come under Young Master Wen's direct orders to demand that Madam Yu punish this boy severely, setting an example for the rest of the Yunmeng Jiang Clan!"

Jiang Cheng pleaded, "A-Niang..."

"Silence!" Madam Yu barked.

Seeing Madam Yu’s reaction, Wang Lingjiao beamed with satisfaction. "This Wei Ying... if memory serves, he's merely a servant of the Jiang Clan, yes? With Sect Leader Jiang absent, I trust Madam Yu understands the gravity of the situation. Otherwise, if the Yunmeng Jiang Clan insists on harboring him, people might begin to wonder... whether certain unsavory rumors... hold some truth after all... Heehee."

Perched in Jiang Fengmian’s usual seat, she covered her lips, giggling coquettishly. Madam Yu’s gaze shifted toward her, dark as an approaching tempest.

Catching the loaded implication, Jiang Cheng bristled, "What rumors?!"

Wang Lingjiao chuckled maliciously, "What rumors do you think? Just a few vintage romantic debts of your dear father's..."

Hearing this woman dare slander Jiang Fengmian right to their faces, fury scorched Wei Wuxian’s chest. "You filthy—"

A sudden, blinding agony tore across his back, and his knees buckled instantly beneath him.

Madam Yu had struck him with Zidian.

Jiang Cheng cried out, "A-Niang!"

Madam Yu rose to her feet, Zidian uncoiling into a crackling whip of vicious purple lightning dancing between her jade-pale fingers. She roared, "Out of the way, Jiang Cheng, or you kneel right beside him!"

Wei Wuxian forced himself up on trembling hands, shouting, "Jiang Cheng, get back! Stay out of this!"

Madam Yu loosed another vicious lash, the strike slamming him flat against the floorboards. She ground out through clenched teeth, "...I told you! You undisciplined, reckless wretch! Sooner or later, you were going to drag this family into ruin!"

Wei Wuxian shoved Jiang Cheng away, clenching his jaw as he took the blows in silence, refusing to flinch or make a sound. In the past, while Madam Yu’s tongue was laced with venom, she had never truly beaten him within an inch of his life; at most, she’d flick him a couple of times before ordering him to kneel and reflect, knowing Jiang Fengmian would release him shortly after. But today, the lash rained down dozens of times in merciless succession. Searing fire tore across his back, his entire body going numb with agonizing pain. Yet he had to swallow it. If the punishment didn't satisfy Wang Lingjiao, if it didn't appease the Qishan Wen Clan, this nightmare would never end!

Wang Lingjiao watched the spectacle with a radiant, satisfied smile.

Once the beating finished, Zidian snapped back into its ring. Wei Wuxian knelt on the stone, his torso swaying violently as if on the verge of collapsing. Jiang Cheng lunged to catch him, but Madam Yu snapped, "Step back! Don't you dare touch him!"

Jinzhu and Yinzhu clamped their hands around Jiang Cheng’s shoulders, holding him fast. Wei Wuxian held on for a few agonizing seconds before crashing heavily against the floor, lying motionless.

Wang Lingjiao blinked in surprise. "That's it?"

Madam Yu sneered, "What else did you expect?"

"Just a few lashes?"

Madam Yu’s brows shot up. "What do you mean, 'just a few lashes'?! What caliber of spiritual weapon do you take Zidian for?! After a flogging like that, he won't be out of bed for a month!"

Wang Lingjiao drawled, "Well, he'll still heal eventually, won't he?"

Jiang Cheng roared, "What more do you want?!"

Wang Lingjiao put on a face of dainty concern. "Madam Yu, if it's meant to be a punishment, it must leave a lesson carved into his bones for the rest of his life—something to ensure he repents forever and never dares cross the line again. If he just takes a beating, rests for a few weeks, and bounces right back onto his feet, how can you call that discipline? Boys his age have terrible memories; the moment the scars fade, they forget the pain entirely. It's completely useless."

Madam Yu’s voice was flat. "What do you propose? Severing both his legs so he can't bounce around anymore?"

Wang Lingjiao smiled sweetly, "Young Master Wen is merciful; he wouldn't dream of demanding something so barbaric as cutting off both legs. Merely lopping off his right hand will settle the debt once and for all."

The truth was laid bare: this woman was purely riding Wen Chao’s coattails, using his authority to settle a petty, personal vendetta against Wei Wuxian for that palm strike in the subterranean cave!

Madam Yu cast a sideways glance down at Wei Wuxian. "Sever his right hand?"

"Precisely."

Yu Ziyuan rose slowly, pacing around Wei Wuxian’s fallen form, seemingly turning the proposition over in her mind.

The agony radiating through Wei Wuxian’s back was so blinding he couldn't even lift his chin. Breaking free of the handmaidens' grip, Jiang Cheng dropped to his knees with a heavy thud, throwing himself over Wei Wuxian’s body. "A-Niang! A-Niang, please don't... It didn't happen the way she claims at all..."

Wang Lingjiao pitched her voice high: "Young Master Jiang, are you accusing me of fibrillation?"

Sprawled flat on the cold floorboards, unable to even roll over, Wei Wuxian’s mind spun: What did she just say? Then the realization hit: She meant 'fabrication'! This woman used to be a maidservant; she can barely read, yet she insists on throwing around fancy prose to sound cultured, butchering the characters!

In a moment of life-or-death peril, the sheer absurdity of human nature was fascinating—the more desperate the crisis, the harder it was to focus, the mind latching onto the most bizarre, irrelevant details. The sheer ridiculousness of her slip actually dragged a silent, hysterical laugh from his throat.

Oblivious to her own humiliation, Wang Lingjiao pressed on, "Madam Yu, think carefully. The Qishan Wen Clan will not let this drop. Cut off this hand and let me take it back to settle the score, and your Yunmeng Jiang Clan can remain peaceful. Otherwise, the next time Young Master Wen comes calling, it won't be settled this easily!"

A terrifying, razor-thin gleam flashed across Madam Yu’s eyes. Her voice dropped to a sinister whisper: "Jinzhu. Yinzhu. Go. Bar the doors. We wouldn't want outsiders catching sight of the blood."

The handmaidens obeyed without a second thought. Answering with a crisp, unified "Yes!", they swung the heavy double doors shut, dropping the iron latch into place.

Hearing the heavy thud of the doors sealing out the daylight, cold dread seized Wei Wuxian’s heart: Is she actually going to cut my hand off?!

Jiang Cheng panicked, throwing his arms around his mother’s knees. "A-Niang! A-Niang, what are you doing?! You can't take his hand!"

After the initial wave of shock, Wei Wuxian clenched his jaw, a ruthless resolve setting into his bones: ...Fine! If a single hand can buy peace for Lotus Pier... then take the damn hand! Worst case, I'll learn to wield a sword with my left!

Wang Lingjiao clapped her hands in delight. "Madam Yu, I knew you were the most loyal subject of our Qishan Wen Clan! Men, pin this brat down!"

Madam Yu said coldly, "There is no need for your men to dirty their hands."

As Jinzhu and Yinzhu stepped forward, Wang Lingjiao chuckled, "Oh, having your own maidservants hold him down? That works too."

Jiang Cheng’s voice broke into desperate sobs. "A-Niang! A-Niang, listen to me, I beg you! Don't do this! If Father finds out..."

If he hadn't brought up Jiang Fengmian, things might have stayed on the razor's edge; the moment the name left his lips, Madam Yu’s face twisted with incandescent fury. She roared, "Don't you dare speak his name! What if he finds out?! What is he going to do—kill me?!"

Wang Lingjiao chimed in happily, "Madam Yu, I truly admire you! It seems you and I will get along splendidly once the Supervisory Office is established!"

Madam Yu yanked her purple silk hem from Jiang Cheng’s desperate grip, turning around slowly. Her brow arched with deadly precision. "Supervisory Office?"

Wang Lingjiao smiled sweetly. "Why, yes! The Supervisory Office. That is the second matter of business bringing me to Yunmeng. The Qishan Wen Clan has issued a new supervisory decree: every major city across the realm will establish an outpost. I hereby declare that from this day forward, Lotus Pier shall serve as the Wen Clan's Supervisory Office in Yunmeng."

No wonder she had strutted around Lotus Pier as if she owned the place—she had already claimed the entire compound as her personal territory!

Jiang Cheng’s eyes burned scarlet. "What damn Supervisory Office?! This is my home!!!"

Wang Lingjiao frowned with petty disgust. "Madam Yu, you really must discipline your son. For centuries, every clan under heaven has bowed before the Wen Clan. In the presence of an imperial envoy, how dare he babble about 'my home' and 'your home'? Truth be told, I was hesitant at first—Lotus Pier is so horribly aged, and it harbors traitors to boot; I doubted whether it was worthy of shouldering such an honor. But seeing how obediently you follow my commands, and finding your temper quite to my liking, I have decided to bestow this glory upon—"

Before the final syllable could clear her throat, Madam Yu’s palm cracked across her face in a deafening, thunderous slap!

The sheer, explosive force sent Wang Lingjiao spinning through the air like a broken top before crashing violently onto the flagstones. Blood gushed from her nose, her wide eyes glazed with absolute shock.

Inside the hall, a dozen Wen disciples drew their swords in unison. Madam Yu gave a dismissive flick of her wrist; Zidian lashed out in a blinding halo of crackling purple lightning, dropping the entire squad into a groaning heap of paralyzed limbs.

With terrifying, regal grace, Madam Yu stepped up to Wang Lingjiao, looking down at her like a piece of filth. Bending low, her hand clamped into Wang Lingjiao’s hair, yanking her head back before delivering another savage, bone-rattling slap across her cheek!

"Insolent wench—how dare you!"

Madam Yu’s patience had shattered long ago; her face was an unmasked tempest of feral fury, inches from Wang Lingjiao's battered face. Paralyzed with terror, her cheek swelling purple, Wang Lingjiao shrieked at the top of her lungs.

Madam Yu cut the scream short with a third brutal backhand, roaring:

"Even when beating a dog, one must look to see who its master is! You dare barge through my gates, stand in my hall, and demand to discipline a member of my household right to my face?! What kind of trash are you to run wild on my grounds?!"

She flung Wang Lingjiao’s head aside like a soiled rag. Producing a pristine silk handkerchief, she meticulously wiped her fingers as if brushing off sewage. Behind her, Jinzhu and Yinzhu wore identical, cold sneers.

Trembling violently, Wang Lingjiao clutched her battered face, tears and snot streaming down her cheeks. "You... you dare lay a hand on me?! The Qishan Wen Clan... and the Yingchuan Wang Clan will never let you off for this!"

Madam Yu tossed the handkerchief to the floor, planting a ruthless kick into her ribs that sent her tumbling across the floor.

"Shut your filthy mouth!" Madam Yu spat, her voice ringing through the rafters. "You common slave! My Meishan Yu Clan has dominated the cultivation realm for centuries, and I have never once heard of a pathetic 'Yingchuan Wang Clan'! What gutter did an upstart peasant family like yours crawl out of?! Is your whole bloodline made of trash like you?! You dare preach to me about master and servant?! Allow me to teach you what true hierarchy looks like!

"I am the master—and you are the dirt beneath my feet!"

Off to the side, Jiang Cheng had half-hauled Wei Wuxian upright from the floorboards.

Watching the storm unfold, both boys were struck completely dumb.
